messages:
laura: heads up — I found a customer case where tokens were charged twice on a resumed streaming request when prefetch ran concurrently. reproducer attached.
aj: can you paste the logs? curious if it's router attribution vs ledger duplication :thinking:
laura: sure, snippet:
```
2026-03-21T12:00:02Z [router] route=resume session=abc prefix_len=128 event=prefix_charge id=tx-9a
2026-03-21T12:00:02Z [prefetch] session=abc prefix_len=128 event=prefetch_charge id=tx-9b
2026-03-21T12:00:02Z [ledger] session=abc record=provisional token_count=128
2026-03-21T12:00:02Z [ledger] session=abc record=confirmed token_count=128
```
laura: both provisional and confirmed show the same prefix amount.
chip: hmm. sounds like attribution runs in two places — router marks resume prefix, prefetch also creates a provisional charge. if both later reconcile to confirmed we double-credit.
maria: can we check sampling/trace id? query to run quickly:
```
SELECT trace_id, event_type, timestamp
FROM token_events
WHERE session_id = 'abc'
ORDER BY timestamp;
```
vik: console shows one event tagged as "prefetch" and one as "resume" under the same session. billing ledger counts both. billing-bot: alert generated: billing-discrepancy session=abc amount=+128 tokens.
aj: is this only when prefetch runs right after resume handshake? or any concurrency? laura: reproduced when prefetch worker (sidecar) races with router on resume path. timing window ~10-50ms.
chip: probable fix: make prefetch idempotent by checking if resume already claimed prefix tokens (session-level marker), or change ledger flow to dedupe provisional->confirmed merges.
maria: UX angle: console rollout for canary should show provisional vs confirmed breakdown per session. current UI groups them and makes it hard to spot duplicates.
laura: quick mitigation — we can treat provisional credit from prefetch as low-priority and delay confirming until a rendezvous check with router state. but that adds latency for background prefetch metrics.
aj: can we add a short-lived session lock in router that prefetch checks? cheap in-memory token. if exists, prefetch should skip prefix charge.
chip: beware of scalability — locks across multi-region. maybe use tag in routing metadata propagated to prefetch sidecars.
vik: I'll surface this in the billing slack with the logs. for next steps: 1) add trace/query (maria) 2) design idempotency check (chip + aj) 3) console tweak to surface provisional vs confirmed (maria) 4) mitigation PR to deprioritize prefetch confirm (laura)
laura: thanks — filing a short RFC and a canary plan. ping me if anyone wants to pair on the repro. :thumbsup:
